bib.title: RAG Inference Pipeline (LLM Engineer's Handbook, ch. 9)

question: How do you build a production RAG inference pipeline (retrieval, prompt augmentation, LLM call) with advanced retrieval techniques?
contributions: Modular ContextRetriever combining self-querying, query expansion, filtered vector search and cross-encoder reranking
A five-line rag() function gluing retrieval, prompt and a SageMaker-hosted LLM
Proposed improvements: conversation memory, routing, hybrid search with BM25, multi-index vectors

method.summary: Describes and codes a RAG inference pipeline: self-query metadata extraction, query expansion, filtered Qdrant search per data category, dedupe, cross-encoder rerank, then prompt build and call to a SageMaker-hosted fine-tuned LLM.

datasets.name: LLM Twin vector DB (articles, posts, repositories)
datasets.source: populated by the chapter 4 feature pipeline

other.use: query expansion and self-query via OPENAI_MODEL_ID

inference.prompting: zero-shot query expansion prompt; few-shot (3 examples) self-query prompt; final prompt 'You are a content creator...' with User query and Context
inference.retrieval: Qdrant filtered vector search, k=3 default, k // 3 per category over 3 categories, expand_to_n_queries=3, rerank to top k

prompts.text: You are an AI language model assistant. Your task is to genera
You are a content creator. Write what the user asked you to while using the provide

results.claim: Query expansion uses GPT-4o-mini at temperature 0 with a zero-shot prompt; the original query is kept and expand_to_n-1 variants are added.
results.quote:
We initialize the ChatOpenAI model with the specified settings and
set the temperature to 0 for deterministic output.

results.claim: Each of N expanded queries searches three data categories, retrieving k // 3 per category, so at most K chunks per search; results are deduplicated and reranked to top K.
results.setup: ContextRetriever.search, defaults k=3, expand_to_n_queries=3; _search asserts k >= 3
results.quote: Thus, we retrieve a maximum of K / 3 items for each data category

results.claim: Reranking scores (query, chunk) pairs with a cross-encoder from sentence_transformers and keeps keep_top_k; model id comes from settings, not named in the chapter.
results.quote:
We will leverage a neural cross-encoder model to compute the score, a value between 0
and 1

results.claim: The chapter reports no retrieval or answer-quality measurements; the LLM was not tested because deployment comes in chapter 10.
results.quote:
Unfortunately, we won’t be able to test out the LLM until we finish
Chapter 10

results.claim: Filtered vector search narrows the search space with metadata (author_id), claimed to improve both accuracy and latency; no numbers given.
results.quote:
Additionally, filtered vector search improves latency by reducing the
number of comparisons the algorithm needs to perform.

results.claim: Hybrid search runs vector and BM25 in parallel, normalises scores, merges by weighted sum; proposed as an improvement, not implemented.
results.quote: Score normalization: The results from both searches are assigned rel

limits: No evaluation of retrieval quality, latency or answer quality; all techniques are described and coded, not measured.
Cross-encoder model id, embedding model, and Qdrant settings are in .env/settings and not given in the chapter.
Chapter notes GPT-4o-mini may be deprecated; model is set via OPENAI_MODEL_ID.
Router, memory, hybrid search and multi-index are proposals, not implemented (multi-index shown as a Superlinked snippet).
practices: Split RAG into retrieval, prompt augmentation and generation; spend most effort on retrieval (intro).
Use the same embedding class at ingestion and query time (Implementing the retrieval module).
Run expanded-query searches in a thread pool to cut latency (ContextRetriever.search).
Deduplicate aggregated results before reranking (Fig 9.3 text).
Retrieve more than K chunks and rerank to the top K; combine with query expansion (reranking section).
Keep a mock flag on each RAG step to cut cost while debugging (RAGStep).
Extract metadata (author) with an LLM and use it as a hard filter (self-querying).
Add a router to skip categories, hybrid BM25 search, and conversation memory (last K or summary plus last K) as improvements.
Build an end-to-end solution first, then iterate (closing section).

terms.definition: Using an LLM to generate multiple queries based on your initial question; also known as multi-query
Use an LLM to extract metadata (tags, IDs, etc.) from the query and use it alongside vector search as filters
Vector search restricted by metadata criteria, reducing the search space before computing similarities
Order all N x K retrieved chunks by relevance to the initial question, keeping the top K
